items.t: Regulator: in British Columbia, real estate trading services are regulated by the BC Financial Services Authority (BCFSA), and BCFSA states a licensed professional must give consumers information about commissions and fees, must only work for either the buyer or the seller in a transaction, must inform consumers of the duties owed to clients and non-clients, and must inform unrepresented consumers of the risks of dealing with a professional representing another party; a professional also cannot represent both buyer and seller in the same transaction (dual agency, prohibited in B.C.
This bio page is evidence of nothing but itself.

The page carries two different "top" formulations side by side. "Top 1%" in the narrative and "#8 out of 5,061" in the bullets appear together with no date or source attached to either beyond the one ranking line — a careful reader should ask which set, which period and which publisher each figure comes from.

The page's framing geography and its stated current base differ. The headline frames Jared as a South Surrey Realtor; the body states he lived in South Surrey for years, lived in Downtown Vancouver's Yaletown, and is now based in Brookswood, Langley, and was raised on a Langley farm — the farm background is the stated source of the farm/acreage specialty the page claims.
Whether the "2026 year-to-date" ranking line is current is itself unverified.

The areas named on the page: South Surrey, Langley, White Rock, Surrey, Brookswood, Cloverdale, Ladner, Tsawwassen "and communities across the Fraser Valley" — as the page states them. The page has no area sections and no links from the body into specific area pages, so this list is the page's whole treatment of areas: a service-area claim, not area content.

items.t: : the page states "#1 at Royal LePage Little Oak Realty, 2025 and 2026 year-to-date"; "Top 1% Fraser Valley Realtor®"; "11+ years of experience and more than $500M in career real estate sales"; and a bulleted list reading "#1 Agent at Royal LePage Little Oak Realty," "#8 out of 5,061 REALTORS® – Fraser Valley," "Top 1% of all REALTORS® – Fraser Valley," "Top 10 Individual Dollar Volume – Fraser Valley," "Top 35 Under 35 – Royal LePage Canada," and "Top 10 – Royal LePage British Columbia." Flagged against the owner-approved set (REALTOR since 2015; 10 straight years FVREB Medallion Club; Top 1% of Fraser Valley Realtors; #1 in South Surrey/White Rock by MLS points for 2025 and 2026 YTD; more than $500M in sales): the page's "#1 at Royal LePage Little Oak Realty" line, the "#8 of 5,061" line and the "Top 35 Under 35" line are OUTSIDE the approved set, and the page carries NO Medallion Club line at all — the approved set's 10-straight-years Medallion Club claim does not appear on this page. Independent verification of any page figure: Not verified — no board, brokerage or Royal LePage source confirming any ranking, sales-volume or award figure was opened.

: general PTT rates are 1% on the first $200,000, 2% to $2 million, 3% above $2 million, plus a further 2% on the residential portion above $3 million; the tax is based on fair market value on the day the transfer is registered at the Land Title Office unless an exemption applies, and in most cases transfers are completed by a legal professional. Worked examples, inputs + tier math stated (fully residential, no exemption unless stated): $500,000 → $2,000 + $6,000 = $8,000; $700,000 → $2,000 + $10,000 = $12,000; $800,000 → $2,000 + $12,000 = $14,000 (fully-qualifying first-time buyer: $6,000); $1,500,000 → $2,000 + $26,000 = $28,000; $1,800,000 → $2,000 + $32,000 = $34,000; $3,500,000 → $2,000 + $36,000 + $45,000 + $10,000 (further 2% tier) = $93,000.

Two different "top" formulations sit side by side with no source: "Top 1%" in the narrative and "#8 out of 5,061" in the bullets, with no date or source attached to either beyond the "#1 … 2025 and 2026 year-to-date" line — and no claim on the page carries a board name for the ranking set or an as-of date other than that one line.

faq.q: What protections do I have when I hire a real estate professional in BC?
faq.a: BCFSA states a licensed professional must give consumers information about commissions and fees, inform them of the duties owed to clients and non-clients, inform unrepresented consumers of the risks of dealing with a professional representing another party, disclose at the outset whether they can represent you and how to complain to BCFSA, and work for only the buyer or the seller in a transaction.

faq.q: What will a purchase cost me in transfer tax?
faq.a: At typical Fraser Valley prices the general property transfer tax runs in the 1% and 2% tiers on fair market value at registration (1% to $200,000, 2% to $2 million, 3% above, plus a further 2% on the residential portion above $3 million), and transfers are in most cases completed by a legal professional. Exemptions are in.
